title: Mixed-cup RingedNormalization
statement:
Fix the stages, operations, cohomology and scalar changes of [def-sf-mixed-cup-coefficient-data] and the normalized point scalar coordinates of [def-sf-mixed-cup-normalized-scalars]. The ringed stages are exactly finite and completed integral stages. Their forgetful functors are the existing ambient inclusions. For an arbitrary finite-ring map, integral reduction or completed integral inclusion, identify the given scalar functor with the actual ringed derived extension: by identity at finite stages, the recorded finite-reduction identification, or the pure-tensor/counit-normalized integral transport of [def-pur-operation-scalar-transport] and its constructible restriction [def-sf-constructible-operation-scalar-transport]. Such integral transports exist. Completed direct image agrees with the ringed structural direct image.

For either support choice use the operation normalizations of [def-pod-mixed-support-cup-product] to identify the actual sheaf cohomology functor with the ambient ringed direct image, or the compactification functor $Rp_*j_!$ of [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data]. At integral compact support use its fixed finite-reduction-normalized recorded identification [def-sf-compact-support-scalar-tensor-identification]. A family $u_c,u_o$ is ringed-normalized precisely when, on every input and each of the three elementary ringed passages, its component, conjugated by these fixed operation and scalar identifications and the point-section identifications, equals the actual ordinary scalar/direct-image counit mate, or respectively the actual proper/open scalar composite. The point scalar factor is the unique map already specified by ordinary balancing and derived counits. This is a component equality, not existence of an arbitrary commuting comparison. The recorded construction data used here is that of [def-sf-operation-stages]. The finite scalar/image identifications are those of [def-pur-finite-compact-support-scalar-data]; the ordinary and proper/open counit mates are those of [def-sp-coefficient-mate-comparisons]; the finite-Tor inclusion and the coefficient-prime unit are those of [def-sf-finite-tor-integral-inclusion].

proof.text: For ringedSource and ringedTarget, inspect the finite, reduction and integral constructors of RingedPassage. In each case IsRinged reduces to True at the indicated endpoint, so True.intro supplies the proof.

Equip the two small finite coefficient fields FieldAt C F and FieldAt C G with the spectral norm and its NormedAlgebra structure over Padic C.l. These structures retain the existing Field and Algebra data. Apply CompactSupportCondensedRealization.scalarModelTransport_nonempty to the recorded coefficient inclusion and W. Its conclusion is exactly scalarTransport_exists, with both the pure-tensor and universal-derived-counit normalizations.

For integralPush_eq, the pull map of the completed coefficient system is the inverse adjunction image of sfCompletedCoefficientMap. Equiv.apply_symm_apply identifies its direct-image adjunct with sfCompletedCoefficientMap. Unfold the two ordinary module direct images; after this adjunct equality they are the same SheafOfModules.pushforward. Congruence for rightDerivedFunctor gives the required equality of derived functors.
